response.markdown_report:
The strongest early direction remains **inference-aligned terminal-mask training**, supported by diagnostics that verify BERT4Rec semantics. No experimental results are available; benefits remain hypotheses.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Sampled margins measure local separation, not pinned HR@10. Empty probes require unavailable values and counts. (2) Bidirectional attention requires explicit supervision/corruption masks; positive IDs alone cannot establish target concealment. (3) Feedback suggests broad relevance displaces specific matches, but does not establish ownership, compatibility, mood, or immediate intent.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) already includes terminal-only masking; originality lies in controlled adaptation, not invention. Its [generator](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data_fin.py) separates target-selection density from replacement probability. (2) [Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) motivate separating margins from benchmark selection; [TemProxRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09784) motivates temporal sensitivity probes without establishing intent. (3) [RankMe](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/garrido23a.html) supports spectral diagnostics: mean cosine alone cannot establish collapse or popularity bias.

**Framework and directions.** Use three layers: semantic correctness → training/inference alignment → behavioral sensitivity. Audit visibility/readout, vary terminal supervision, then compare matched recent/older deletions. Complement cosine with centered variance, singular-value effective rank and training-frequency exposure correlations; distinguish observations from causal explanations. HR@10 remains the selection criterion.

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/implementation difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder. Assessments cover all three dimensions.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Target-visibility audit [BERT4Rec] | 3/7/3 | Reusable correctness evidence; inexpensive | Established verification; indirect ranking benefit; sampler tracing required |
| Terminal-mask sampling [BERT4Rec] | 3/7/4 | Feasible alignment ablation with useful follow-ups | Incremental; baseline-dependent benefit; supervision weighting requires care |
| Recent/older deletion probe [TemProxRec] | 4/6/4 | Practical temporal sensitivity evidence | Descriptive; uncertain ranking benefit; matching deletions requires care |

**Selected algorithm.** Define α as the example-level probability of terminal-only versus baseline random-position masking. Inspect baseline α first; compare it with 0.5, or 0 if already 0.5. Prespecify this single alternative. Keep window sampling, corruption policy, random-mask density, optimizer and loss reduction fixed; terminal-only examples necessarily change target counts.

```text
sample a training-only window using the baseline sampler
with probability α:
    save its terminal item; replace that position with MASK
    supervise only that position; left-pad consistently
otherwise:
    apply baseline random masking and supervision
optimize baseline loss on supervised positions
```

Audit shifted-target leakage, padding attention, final-nonpadding readout and predictor parity. Repeated genuine occurrences are legitimate context; optional unchanged/random replacements require separate accounting. Log targets, windows, updates and GPU seconds: equal epochs need not imply equal supervision. A later terminal-versus-one-random-target control matches target count but still changes right-context availability. Density tuning is separate.

Preserve seeds 0/42, 200 epochs maximum, 200 batches/epoch, routing, DATA_DIR, ModelView, diagnostic entry points and predictor consistency. Train one model/category; select by pinned macro validation HR@10. Report category effects and exploratory paired uncertainty. Validation reuse risks selection overfitting; popularity shortcuts require separate evidence. Make fixed-budget claims, not convergence claims ([replicability study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07483)).

idea.description: Test one prespecified change to the example-level probability of terminal-only masked supervision in the supplied BERT4Rec baseline, retaining its random masked-item objective for remaining examples.
idea.motivation: Terminal-only supervision matches appended-mask next-item inference and is feasible at this early research stage. It does not directly encode compatibility or current intent, and its published antecedent limits originality. Whether it improves next-item ranking must be determined by the unchanged host validation evaluator.
idea.implementation_notes: Inspect the supplied corrected baseline during implementation; no baseline probability or corruption policy has been established in this report. Define alpha as the fraction of sampled examples assigned terminal-only supervision, distinct from random target-selection density and conditional replacement probability. Compare baseline alpha with 0.5; if baseline alpha is already 0.5, use 0.0 as the single prespecified alternative. Do not infer baseline alpha from the original implementation's ten random copies plus one terminal copy: its nominal 1/11 example fraction is not necessarily its target-level loss fraction. Sample the same training-only windows using identical truncation and positional conventions. Terminal examples replace the window's final original item with the reserved MASK and supervise only that position. Genuine repeated occurrences elsewhere remain valid context. Preserve baseline random corruption, optimizer, batch size, updates and loss reduction; record their exact settings and supervised-target counts. Do not average loss over padding. If the baseline uses batch-wide target averaging, acknowledge that changing target counts changes relative example weighting; do not silently replace this reduction. A subsequent one-target-per-sequence control can compare terminal and uniformly sampled random positions, but constitutes a separate experiment and still confounds target location with available right context. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum epochs 200 and batches per epoch 200. Record actual updates, sequence presentations, supervised tokens and GPU seconds; preserve the shared search budget. Use exactly one independently trained BERT4Rec model/checkpoint per category, without fusion or averaging. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath the trial directory and retain all four routes. Synchronize the predictor writer, working/predict.py, configuration and checkpoint. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) and the host ModelView interfaces. Diagnose selected supervised positions using sampler bookkeeping without changing the loader's required tuple; separately report replacement branches and empty-probe counts. Verify padding-key masking, final-nonpadding readout and exclusion of padding/mask from candidate scoring. Report cosine as directional alignment, not conclusive collapse. For fixed real-item samples and appended-mask user representations, report raw norms, centered variance and centered singular-value spectra separately; define RankMe effective rank as exp(-sum(p*log(p))) with p=sigma/sum(sigma), rather than squared-singular-value entropy. Zero spectra are unavailable. Popularity associations use training counts only and establish correlation, not causation. Keep twenty-user full-catalog unseen-item audits separate from validation HR@10; unidentified items remain unassessable. Use only available histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions. Report category HR@10 and macro effects; paired user bootstrap intervals, if host per-user validation outcomes are available, are exploratory and conditional on fixed models/candidates. Never substitute local metrics for host selection or read hidden test data.
idea.pseudocode:
Read corrected baseline configuration and identify alpha0, random masking, loss reduction and window sampler.
Set alpha1 = 0.5 if alpha0 != 0.5 else 0.0 before observing candidate validation results.
For each authorized baseline/candidate training run, reset prescribed seeds:
  For each sampled training-only window:
    Draw terminal_only with probability alpha.
    If terminal_only:
      Save the original terminal item as target.
      Replace its position with reserved MASK.
      Mark only that position supervised.
    Else:
      Apply unchanged baseline random masking and retain explicit supervision/corruption bookkeeping.
    Apply baseline truncation, left padding and position conventions consistently.
  Optimize unchanged baseline loss over supervised positions.
  Count windows, targets, updates and GPU seconds.
Before host evaluation:
  Audit absence of shifted-label exposure; distinguish intentional corruption branches and repeated items.
  Verify final readout uses max(where(sequence != 0)), including appended MASK.
  Verify candidate IDs exclude padding and MASK.
  Verify checkpoint-loaded embedded predictor matches training-side evaluation scores within a recorded numerical tolerance.
  Return measured diagnostic metrics and explicit definitions; mark empty measurements unavailable.
Run unchanged host validation; compare four-category macro HR@10 and category effects.
Retain exactly one selected checkpoint per category; do not combine predictions.

originality.positive: Pairs a precisely defined sampling ablation with family-specific correctness and supervision accounting.
originality.negative: Terminal-only examples are already part of BERT4Rec; changing their frequency is incremental.

future_potential.positive: A controlled result can motivate separate studies of target location, supervision density and temporal sensitivity.
future_potential.negative: The baseline may already provide adequate alignment, and this change does not directly resolve compatibility or immediate-intent failures.

code_difficulty.positive: The core change is a sampler probability and retains the existing backbone and scoring function.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable implementation requires corruption bookkeeping, loss-weight accounting and predictor/checkpoint parity checks.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item modeling and appended-mask next-item inference.
Includes terminal-only masked examples; reports dataset-dependent mask proportions.
limitations: Does not establish an optimal terminal-example fraction for these four datasets.
Terminal-versus-interior supervision also changes available right context.

related_work.title: Official BERT4Rec training-data generator
contributions: Separates target-selection density from conditional replacement probability.
Implements random corrupted copies and additional terminal-only examples.
limitations: Example fractions do not establish target-level loss contributions.
Its defaults must not be assumed to match the supplied corrected baseline.

related_work.title: Official BERT4Rec training implementation
contributions: Provides executable masked-target loss normalization for reproducibility.
limitations: Batch-wide target averaging weights variable-target-count examples differently from per-sequence averaging.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can produce inconsistent model comparisons.
limitations: Does not predict whether this training change improves the pinned benchmark.
Does not authorize changing its mandatory evaluator.

related_work.title: TemProxRec
contributions: Motivates examining temporal information beyond interaction order.
limitations: Temporal sensitivity cannot establish ownership, mood or immediate need.

related_work.title: RankMe: Assessing the Downstream Performance of Pretrained Self-Supervised Representations by Their Rank
contributions: Defines an effective-rank measure using entropy of normalized singular values.
limitations: Does not supply universal collapse thresholds or establish recommendation quality.
Centering and normalization choices affect interpretation.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec replicability study
contributions: Demonstrates that training duration can materially affect reproduced BERT4Rec performance.
limitations: Its reported compute requirements do not establish requirements for these datasets.
Longer-training findings do not override the prescribed search budget or epoch ceiling.
